item.title: US earn narrow win over Italy at 'most challenging' World Cup
item.description: The U.S. survived a tough test against Italy at the FIBA Women's World Cup on Sunday, with their narrow 55-52 victory serving as a further sign of growing competitiveness in the women's game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. survived a tough test against Italy at the FIBA Women's World Cup on Sunday, with their narrow 55-52 victory serving as a further sign of growing competitiveness in the women's game. Italy held the U.S. to their lowest points total in 42 years and were up 50-48 with less than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter before the defending champions turned things around to book their spot in the quarter-finals. "I think this is the most challenging World Cup to win of any one before because of how good everyone is," U.S. coach Kara Lawson told reporters post-game in Berlin. "There's much more depth to the rosters at the World Cup. There's players that can come in off the bench and change games and we saw that for Italy tonight. We've seen that throughout the tournament." On Saturday, Mali earned just their second victory at the tournament with a shock 82-73 win over Spain, who had been [USN:L6N44U1ET TEXT:"widely expected"] to enjoy a deep run. "Every game feels like a dog fight. It's really hard," said Lawson. "And on any given night, if you're not prepared to play, you'll lose. That's awesome for our sport." Jackie Young led the U.S. with 10 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Angel Reese put up eight points, three rebounds, two blocks and a steal, with Lawson calling the Atlanta Dream forward a "difference maker". "She comes into the game and she plays with great energy and she competes," Lawson said of the 24 -year-old. "She scores, she rebounds, she plays with great pace. It's what you want in a young player to come in and do that." Forward Breanna Stewart said the 11-times champions leaned on their experience to grind out a win. "We've all been in these high-stress situations, knowing that the gym is cheering against us. ... And we embraced it," said Stewart, who was proud of the team's resilience. "It's supposed to be challenging, and we're supposed to have moments where we're not at our best," Lawson added. "And the teams that can persevere through that and have a resilient mindset are the ones that are able to win." The U.S. play Czechia next on Monday.

item.title: Cardinals storm past Rockies thanks to big inning, Cooper Hjerpe's debut
item.description: Nolan Gorman homered to cap a six-run fifth inning, Cooper Hjerpe struck out six in four spotless innings in his major league debut and the St. Louis Cardinals beat the Colorado Rockies 10-8 on Sunday in Denver.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nolan Gorman homered to cap a six-run fifth inning, Cooper Hjerpe struck out six in four spotless innings in his major league debut and the St. Louis Cardinals beat the Colorado Rockies 10-8 on Sunday in Denver. Ivan Herrera and Alec Burleson each had three hits and Thomas Saggese and Joshua Baez finished with two hits apiece for St. Louis (72-72), which remained four games behind Arizona for the third National League wild-card berth. George Soriano got the final out for his third save. Hjerpe (1-0), the Cardinals' first-round draft pick in 2022, entered in the fourth and didn't allow a baserunner. Jake McCarthy homered and singled twice, Mickey Moniak also went deep and finished with two hits and four RBIs and TJ Rumfield had three hits for Colorado (55-88). The Rockies jumped ahead in the first inning on a two-out RBI double by Rumfield and a single by Moniak to make it 2-0. The Cardinals got a run in the second when Saggese doubled and scored on Nathan Church's single. The Rockies padded their lead in the third when Cole Carrigg and Rumfield singled and Moniak homered to center to make it 5-1. It was his 22nd of the season. That ended the day for starter Kyle Leahy, who allowed five runs on six hits and struck out six in 2 2/3 innings. He was saved from a loss when his team rallied in the fifth against Tanner Gordon, who allowed five runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings. Herrera started things with a two-out single, Burleson doubled and Jordan Walker loaded the bases with a walk. Leo Bernal laced a single to right to bring home two runs. Baez greeted reliever Jimmy Herget (0-6) with a two-run single to tie the score, and Gorman homered to right to put St. Louis in front. It was his ninth of the season. The Cardinals made it 10-5 in the eighth on a two-run double by Herrera followed by Burleson's single. McCarthy led off the bottom of the inning with his 15th home run and added a two-run single in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reports: Giants agree to 2-year, $13M extension with QB Jameis Winston
item.description: The New York Giants and veteran backup quarterback Jameis Winston have agreed to a two-year, $13 million extension, according to multiple reports on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Giants and veteran backup quarterback Jameis Winston have agreed to a two-year, $13 million extension, according to multiple reports on Sunday. Winston is now under contract with New York through the 2028 season. Winston is the backup behind second-year pro Jaxson Dart but is viewed as a team leader. This is his second campaign with New York; last season, he passed for 567 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in three games (two starts). Winston, 32, is entering his 12th NFL season. He has made 89 career starts, with 70 of them coming for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers from 2015-19. Winston was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 draft by the Buccaneers and was a Pro Bowl selection as a rookie. In his first season with Tampa Bay, Winston set career highs with 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions. The yards and picks were the most in the NFL that season. Winston also has played for the New Orleans Saints (2020-23) and Cleveland Browns (2024). Overall, Winston has passed for 24,792 yards, 156 touchdowns and 113 interceptions in 108 career games (89 starts). He has a 36-53 record as a starting quarterback after dropping both of his starts last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fiorentina sack Grosso after three straight Serie A defeats
item.description: Fiorentina sacked manager Fabio Grosso on Sunday after three successive defeats at the start of the season left them bottom of Serie A, the Italian club said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fiorentina sacked manager Fabio Grosso on Sunday after three successive defeats at the start of the season left them bottom of Serie A, the Italian club said in a statement. Fiorentina lost 4-0 at AS Roma and 3-0 at home to promoted Frosinone before Saturday’s 2-1 home defeat by Torino, leaving them with one goal scored and nine conceded. They visit Venezia on Friday. The 48-year-old former Italy defender had been in charge for less than three months, having replaced Paolo Vanoli on June 8 and signed a two-year contract. Vanoli had guided Fiorentina to a 15th-place finish last season after taking over from Stefano Pioli, who was sacked following a 10-game winless start. Grosso, who scored the winning penalty against France in the 2006 World Cup final, joined Fiorentina after winning promotion with Sassuolo in his first season and guiding them to mid-table in Serie A. He had previously managed Bari, Hellas Verona, Brescia, Sion, Frosinone and Olympique Lyonnais.

item.title: USA-Accident à Miami d'un avion-cargo d'Amazon Prime, cinq morts
item.description: Au moins cinq personnes ont été tuées dimanche à l'aéroport international de Miami après qu'un avion-cargo d'Amazon Prime Air est sorti de piste et s'est écrasé, ont dit les autorités locales, indiquant que toutes les pistes d'atterrissage de l'aéroport ont été fermées à la suite de l'incident.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Au moins cinq personnes ont été tuées dimanche à l'aéroport international de Miami après qu'un avion-cargo d'Amazon Prime Air est sorti de piste et s'est écrasé, ont dit les autorités locales, indiquant que toutes les pistes d'atterrissage de l'aéroport ont été fermées à la suite de l'incident. Cinq personnes ont également été blessées, dont trois se trouvent dans un état grave, ont précisé des représentants locaux lors d'une conférence de presse. Plusieurs véhicules au sol ont été percutés par l'appareil Prime Air quand celui-ci est sorti de piste peu avant 14h00 (18h00 GMT). Via le réseau social X, le secrétaire américain aux Transports, Sean Duffy, a déclaré que toutes les pistes d'atterrissage de l'aéroport international de Miami étaient fermées à 19h00 GMT et que les voyageurs devaient s'"attendre à des retards importants et à de possibles annulations" de vols. L'avion accidenté est un Boeing 767-300 qui était arrivé en provenance de San Juan à Porto Rico, d'après l'administration américaine de l'aviation civile (FAA). Une porte-parole d'Amazon a déclaré que la compagnie de fret aérien 21 Air opérait cet appareil pour Amazon. Aucun commentaire n'a été obtenu dans l'immédiat auprès de 21 Air. "Nous travaillons étroitement avec les responsables et autorités locaux pour comprendre exactement ce qu'il s'est passé", a dit cette porte-parole d'Amazon dans un communiqué. "Pour l'heure, notre priorité absolue est la sécurité et le bien-être de toutes les personnes impliquées". La FAA a fait savoir qu'elle ouvrirait une enquête sur l'accident.

item.title: Jake Burger, Corey Seager guide Rangers past Rays for series split
item.description: Jake Burger homered twice, drove in three runs and scored three times to help the Texas Rangers earn a split of the four-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays with an 8-6 win on Sunday afternoon in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jake Burger homered twice, drove in three runs and scored three times to help the Texas Rangers earn a split of the four-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays with an 8-6 win on Sunday afternoon in Arlington, Texas. Corey Seager also homered, Ezequiel Duran had three hits and an RBI and Logan O'Hoppe delivered two hits and scored twice for the Rangers (71-73), who had lost three of four and trailed 4-0 early on Sunday. Rangers left-hander MacKenzie Gore allowed five runs and six hits in three-plus innings. He struck out one and walked three. Trevor Williams (1-0) followed with two innings of scoreless relief to earn the win. Jakob Junis pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his sixth save. Rays starter Ian Seymour was also limited to three-plus innings, allowing four runs (three earned) and five hits. He struck out two and walked one. Chandler Simpson produced two hits and scored two runs, while Yandy Diaz, Jonathan Aranda and Jonny DeLuca all produced two hits and an RBI for the Rays (85-58), who had won two in a row. The Rays scored four runs on four straight at-bats in the second. Victor Mesa Jr. singled, Nick Fortes followed with a squeeze bunt, Diaz singled and Aranda hit a sacrifice fly for his sixth RBI of the series. Burger led off the bottom of the second with a home run to cut it to 4-1, but Junior Caminero got the run back with a sacrifice fly in the fourth to make it 5-1. Burger launched his second homer of the game in the fourth with a runner aboard to make it 5-3. O'Hoppe followed with a single to end Seymour's day. Steven Matz (5-5) relieved Kevin Kelly later in the inning and Justin Foscue came through with a two-out, two-run double that tied it 5-5. Matz came back out for the fifth and surrendered an RBI single to Elias Diaz for a 6-5 Texas lead. Casey Legumina replaced Matz with two outs and gave up an RBI single to Duran to extend the lead to 7-5. Simpson singled, stole second and scored on a single by DeLuca to cut it to 7-6 in the seventh. Seager gave the Rangers some insurance with a solo home run in the eighth to make it 8-6. --Field Level Media

item.title: Única mujer que compite como directora en Festival de Venecia dice industria sigue siendo desigual
item.description: La escasa presencia de mujeres que optan al primer premio del Festival de Cine de Venecia refleja un problema estructural en la industria cinematográfica, afirmó el domingo la directora danesa May el-Toukhy al presentar su crudo drama "Woman Unknown".
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer
item.content:encoded: La escasa presencia de mujeres que optan al primer premio del Festival de Cine de Venecia refleja un problema estructural en la industria cinematográfica, afirmó el domingo la directora danesa May el-Toukhy al presentar su crudo drama "Woman Unknown". El-Toukhy es la única mujer que dirige un largometraje de ficción entre los 21 candidatos al León de Oro. Solo otra obra a concurso, un documental, cuenta con una codirectora, lo que aviva el debate sobre la representación de las mujeres en el cine. "Es un problema estructural, y es un problema estructural con el que me he topado a lo largo de toda mi carrera", declaró la cineasta danesa-egipcia en una rueda de prensa previa al estreno de su última película. "Me costó muchísimo terminar mi primera película tras graduarme en la escuela de cine. Creo que tardé seis o siete años, mientras que mis compañeros varones fueron mucho más rápidos que yo". El director del festival, Alberto Barberá, ha defendido la programación de este año, señalando que las mujeres dirigieron solo el 24 % de las películas presentadas —una cifra inferior al 30 % del año anterior— y afirmando que las decisiones de selección se basaron en la calidad artística. El-Toukhy señaló que conseguir financiación sigue siendo más difícil para las directoras, lo que afecta a todo, desde los presupuestos hasta las oportunidades de casting y, en última instancia, a las posibilidades de que una película llegue a los principales festivales. "LA INVISIBILIDAD DE LAS MUJERES" Ambientada tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial, "Woman Unknown" narra la historia de Marie, una criada danesa que se prepara para casarse con su acaudalado patrón cuando una relación pasada con un soldado alemán amenaza con destruir su futuro. La película se desarrolla con el telón de fondo de una Dinamarca recién liberada, donde las mujeres acusadas de fraternizar con las fuerzas de ocupación alemanas solían ser sometidas a humillaciones públicas y a la justicia popular. El-Toukhy afirmó que los temas de la historia se hacían eco de sus comentarios sobre la representación. "Mi película trata sobre la invisibilidad de las mujeres", afirmó. "Trata, por un lado, de la cosificación y, por otro, de pasar desapercibidas y carecer de voz". Aunque agradece la atención que ha suscitado su presencia en la competición, afirmó que preferiría que se sumaran más cineastas mujeres. "Por supuesto, me encantaría tener a más colegas mujeres a mi lado en la competición", dijo. "Tras el movimiento #MeToo, todas éramos muy conscientes de este desequilibrio de género, y en los últimos años ha ocurrido algo que nos está haciendo volver, en cierto modo, a cómo eran las cosas antes". La actriz Mathilde Arcel, que interpreta a Marie, señaló que la película arroja luz sobre las mujeres que durante décadas cargaron con el estigma de las relaciones mantenidas en tiempos de guerra. "Hay mujeres que ni siquiera contaron a sus familias que habían vivido estas experiencias", explicó.

item.title: Partido de extrema derecha logra victoria histórica en las elecciones regionales alemanas
item.description: El partido Alternativa para Alemania (AfD) se aupó al primer puesto en las elecciones regionales celebradas el domingo en Sajonia-Anhalt, lo que sitúa a un partido de extrema derecha a las puertas del poder a nivel regional por primera vez desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial, según las encuestas a pie de urna,
item.dc:creator: Miranda Murray, Kirsti Knolle
item.content:encoded: El partido Alternativa para Alemania (AfD) se aupó al primer puesto en las elecciones regionales celebradas el domingo en Sajonia-Anhalt, lo que sitúa a un partido de extrema derecha a las puertas del poder a nivel regional por primera vez desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial, según las encuestas a pie de urna, La AfD obtuvo el 44,4 % de los votos, mientras que los conservadores del canciller Friedrich Merz quedaron muy por detrás, con un 18,3 %, y tanto los socialdemócratas de centroizquierda como los Verdes superaron el umbral mínimo para entrar en el parlamento, según una encuesta a boca de urna de la cadena ARD. A medida que avanzaba el recuento, aún no estaba claro si la AfD había obtenido suficientes votos para conseguir la mayoría absoluta en el parlamento. Pero el significado político más amplio de las elecciones, que registraron una participación superior al 80 %, según la cadena ZDF, era evidente. "Hemos hecho historia en este país", afirmó Ulrich Siegmund, el candidato principal de la AfD en Sajonia-Anhalt, de 35 años, que atrajo a miles de personas a sus mítines de campaña y que en repetidas ocasiones presentó la victoria en el estado como un primer paso para hacerse con el poder a nivel nacional en las elecciones federales previstas para 2029. Su partido quiere restringir drásticamente la inmigración, restablecer los lazos con Rusia, abandonar el euro y promover un patriotismo alemán sin complejos. El resultado supone un importante revés para Merz, cuya popularidad personal se ha hundido hasta mínimos históricos, ya que los votantes han dado la espalda tanto a sus reformas previstas para reactivar la estancada economía alemana como a su estilo de comunicación personal, propenso a los deslizes. La copresidenta del partido AfD, Alice Weidel, celebró un resultado «histórico» que había otorgado a la AfD un claro mandato para gobernar, aunque podría ser necesario un prolongado período de negociaciones para formar una coalición antes de que se consiga una mayoría clara. Todos los partidos mayoritarios se han negado a colaborar con la AfD, que ha sido clasificada como de extrema derecha por la oficina local del servicio de inteligencia interior alemán. No obstante, podría encontrar un socio en el partido de extrema izquierda BSW, si este logra superar el umbral para entrar en el Parlamento. Aunque Sajonia-Anhalt, que anteriormente formaba parte de la Alemania Oriental comunista, es uno de los estados federados más pequeños de Alemania, con una población de poco más de 2 millones de habitantes, el resultado pone de relieve el rápido avance de la AfD desde su creación en 2013. En un panorama político fragmentado, la AfD es ahora el partido más popular de Alemania a nivel nacional, con un 28 % de intención de voto según una reciente encuesta del INSA, muy por delante de los conservadores, que se sitúan en el 20 %. El partido goza de especial popularidad en el este de Alemania. Sin embargo, a principios de año obtuvo alrededor del 20 % en los estados occidentales de Baden-Wurtemberg y Renania-Palatinado, lo que pone de manifiesto su creciente atractivo a nivel nacional.

item.title: Enviados EEUU esperan nuevas conversaciones Ucrania y Rusia después de visitas a ambas capitales
item.description: Los enviados de paz estadounidenses Jared Kushner y Steve Witkoff anunciaron un nuevo impulso en las negociaciones de paz tras reunirse el domingo en Kiev con el presidente ucraniano Volodímir Zelenski, en un momento en que el Gobierno de Trump ha renovado sus esfuerzos por poner fin a la guerra que Rusia lleva librando en Ucrania desde hace cuatro años y medio.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder, Anna Voitenko
item.content:encoded: Los enviados de paz estadounidenses Jared Kushner y Steve Witkoff anunciaron un nuevo impulso en las negociaciones de paz tras reunirse el domingo en Kiev con el presidente ucraniano Volodímir Zelenski, en un momento en que el Gobierno de Trump ha renovado sus esfuerzos por poner fin a la guerra que Rusia lleva librando en Ucrania desde hace cuatro años y medio. Kushner y Witkoff viajaron desde Moscú, donde el sábado mantuvieron tres horas de conversaciones con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, aunque no parecieron lograr ningún avance decisivo en el conflicto. Witkoff, enviado del presidente Donald Trump, afirmó que habían "escuchado nuevas ideas" en Moscú, sin dar más detalles al respecto, y que esperaban que se anunciara "en breve" una nueva ronda de conversaciones entre Ucrania y Rusia mediadas por Estados Unidos. Zelenski elogió la conversación "muy sustantiva" mantenida con Witkoff y Kushner y afirmó que Ucrania estaba preparada para las conversaciones trilaterales. Señaló que también había abordado el tema de los suministros de defensa aérea y el apoyo energético a Ucrania de cara al invierno, ante la expectativa de que Rusia vuelva a bombardear la red eléctrica ucraniana. Las rondas anteriores de conversaciones de paz mediadas por Estados Unidos e impulsadas por Trump —quien basó su campaña en la promesa de poner fin rápidamente a la guerra— han dado pocos resultados. El viernes insinuó que Estados Unidos tenía una nueva propuesta, aunque no dio más detalles. El asesor del Kremlin, Yuri Ushakov, calificó la reunión del sábado de "muy útil", mientras que un funcionario de la Casa Blanca declaró a Reuters que los próximos pasos se anunciarían en las próximas semanas. "Hemos avanzado mucho en Moscú", declaró Witkoff a los periodistas en Kiev el domingo, y añadió que se sentía "muy animado" por sus conversaciones con el equipo ucraniano. El presidente ucraniano, que considera que Washington será clave para cualquier acuerdo de paz, ha afirmado que existe una ventana de oportunidad para alcanzar la paz antes de que Estados Unidos comience a centrarse en sus próximas elecciones presidenciales de 2028. Los enviados estadounidenses mantuvieron varias horas de conversaciones con funcionarios ucranianos. Los asesores de seguridad nacional británicos, franceses y alemanes, que también se encontraban en Kiev, se unieron a la reunión durante la última hora. Estaba previsto que las conversaciones entre Estados Unidos y Ucrania continuaran el domingo por la noche. Durante una pausa, Zelenskiy afirmó que los responsables habían debatido la posibilidad de garantías económicas y de seguridad para Kiev, así como un "plan de prosperidad" para la posguerra. "En los últimos 10 a 12 meses, creo que nos hemos fortalecido", afirmó Zelenski, y añadió que Estados Unidos y Europa lo habían observado. OPTIMISMO CAUTELOSO EN LAS CALLES DE KIEV Witkoff y Kushner, yerno de Trump, han visitado Moscú en varias ocasiones en su calidad de emisarios de paz. Pero el domingo fue su primera visita a Kiev en calidad de negociadores estadounidenses. Los dirigentes ucranianos llevaban tiempo esperando esta visita y, en las calles de Kiev —que ha sufrido intensos bombardeos en las últimas semanas—, algunos residentes se mostraban esperanzados. "El problema se puede resolver en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. Queremos la paz. Yo mismo he combatido, así que sé lo que es la guerra. Necesitamos la paz, porque no hay otra salida", afirmó el veterano militar Stepan Yermak. En conversaciones anteriores, las partes se han mantenido muy alejadas en cuestiones clave, incluido el futuro de la región de Donbás, en el este de Ucrania. Rusia ha exigido la retirada de Ucrania de un cinturón de localidades que aún controla en esa zona, pero Kiev se ha negado, argumentando que aún puede mantener el control. "La cuestión del Donbás… creo que es la cuestión central de esta guerra", declaró Zelenski a periodistas el domingo. Para Ucrania, contar con garantías de seguridad firmes por parte de sus aliados europeos y de Estados Unidos es fundamental para disuadir a Rusia de volver a invadir el país. Aunque afirmó que el tema se había debatido, Zelenski no dio detalles sobre si se habían logrado avances. ALTO EL FUEGO TEMPORAL Aunque las líneas del frente de la guerra terrestre permanecen en gran medida estables, tanto las fuerzas rusas como las ucranianas han intensificado los ataques aéreos de largo alcance en las últimas semanas. Rusia ha bombardeado la capital ucraniana día y noche con misiles y drones durante las últimas dos semanas, incluido un ataque el viernes contra la sede del servicio de seguridad SBU. El Kremlin ha afirmado que suspendería los ataques contra Kiev hasta el lunes, mientras que Zelenski ha declarado que Ucrania también detendría los ataques contra Moscú. Sin embargo, los combates no han cesado a lo largo del frente de 1.200 km (750 millas) y Rusia bombardeó otras ciudades ucranianas el sábado. A lo largo del verano, Ucrania ha asestado golpes devastadores a refinerías rusas, terminales petroleras y los almacenes del minorista online Wildberries, en un intento por encarecer a Moscú la continuación de la guerra. Ucrania afirmó el domingo que había atacado durante la noche la refinería de petróleo de Riazán, situada a unos 480 km (300 millas) dentro de Rusia, provocando un incendio.

item.title: Un Alcaraz en estado de gracia se impone a Paul y clasifica para cuartos de final del Abierto EEUU
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz venció el domingo al estadounidense Tommy Paul, cabeza de serie número 20, por 6-4, 6-3 y 6-4 en un partido de gran intensidad y muchos golpes potentes, con lo que se clasificó para los cuartos de final del Abierto de Estados Unidos y sigue firmemente en la senda de conseguir dos títulos consecutivos en Flushing Meadows.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Carlos Alcaraz venció el domingo al estadounidense Tommy Paul, cabeza de serie número 20, por 6-4, 6-3 y 6-4 en un partido de gran intensidad y muchos golpes potentes, con lo que se clasificó para los cuartos de final del Abierto de Estados Unidos y sigue firmemente en la senda de conseguir dos títulos consecutivos en Flushing Meadows. El siete veces campeón de Grand Slam ha alcanzado su mejor forma en Nueva York tras casi cinco meses de baja por una lesión en la muñeca derecha y ha ampliado a 18 su racha de victorias en torneos de Grand Slam con una impresionante exhibición de golpes frente a otro jugador de gran potencia. "Creo que simplemente he jugado mi juego", afirmó Alcaraz, que seguía luciendo fresco con la equipación personalizada en blanco y negro de Nike que lleva ya por segunda semana. "Intenté jugar según mi estilo. Tommy es un jugador con mucho talento y sus golpes son bastante peligrosos; es difícil controlar la pelota cuando te llega. Estaba preparado para una batalla", agregó. El servicio de Alcaraz se vio bajo presión en el tercer juego cuando Paul lanzó un exquisito golpe ganador de derecha a 100 mph por encima de la red que puso en pie al estadio Arthur Ashe, pero el español se mantuvo firme antes de golpear en el último momento para llevarse el primer set.

item.title: North Korea's Kim Jong Un says new destroyer will be part of nuclear response system
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said the country's newest destroyer would be part of a nuclear response system and could deliver "annihilating retaliatory strikes", state media KCNA reported on Monday, although it did not say whether the vessel would carry nuclear weapons.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said the country's newest destroyer would be part of a nuclear response system and could deliver "annihilating retaliatory strikes", state media KCNA reported on Monday, although it did not say whether the vessel would carry nuclear weapons. North Korea has accelerated efforts to modernise its navy as Kim pursues a broader expansion of the country's nuclear-capable forces. At a commissioning ceremony in the eastern port city of Wonsan on Sunday, Kim said the new ship's deployment to the sea east of the Korean Peninsula sent a clear signal to North Korea's adversaries. "The time has come for us to exercise our sovereignty at sea and under water," Kim said, according to KCNA. The 5,000-ton-class destroyer, the "Kang Kon", is the second warship of its class to enter service, following the commissioning of the "Choe Hyon" destroyer on North Korea's west coast about [USN:L1N42V135 TEXT:"three months earlier"], KCNA cited Kim as saying. Kim said North Korea's naval nuclear armaments were advancing, and the country would continue to expand what he called its most powerful strategic assets in key waters to protect its maritime sovereignty and regional security. He added that the Kang Kon would form part of North Korea's state nuclear response system. KCNA did not specify what weapons systems might be deployed on the Kang Kon, but said is has the same weapons systems as the Choe Hyon. A previous KCNA report said Choe Hyon-class destroyers can carry a range of weapons, including missiles that analysts say are capable of carrying a nuclear payload. Kim said he would demonstrate another stage of North Korea's naval buildup in eight months, KCNA said, without giving details. Kim also said the construction of naval bases on North Korea's east coast was under way and that the country would create new naval units and build different classes of warships.

item.title: Nolan Arenado, Diamondbacks pull out rubber match vs. Astros
item.description: Nolan Arenado slugged his 22nd home run, left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez produced a quality start and the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks claimed the rubber match of a three-game interleague series against the Houston Astros with a 3-2 victory on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nolan Arenado slugged his 22nd home run, left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez produced a quality start and the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks claimed the rubber match of a three-game interleague series against the Houston Astros with a 3-2 victory on Sunday. Arenado spotted the Diamondbacks (76-68) a 3-1 lead in the top of the third inning with his two-run blast off Astros right-hander Peter Lambert (8-8). Rodriguez (15-5) and four Arizona relievers made that advantage stand, though the Astros applied pressure down the stretch. Trailing by two runs entering the eighth, the Astros (73-71) mounted a threat against Arizona reliever Jonathan Loaisiga. Jose Altuve capped a three-hit game by doubling to left with one out and scored after Christian Walker and pinch hitter LaMonte Wade Jr. singled in succession. But Loaisiga rallied by striking out Daulton Varsho before inducing pinch hitter Taylor Trammell to hit a soft liner to Ketel Marte at second, stranding two baserunners and preserving the lead. Right-hander Kevin Ginkel notched his third save by striking out the side in the ninth inning. The Astros took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first when Yordan Alvarez smacked a 1-1 changeup from Rodriguez out to right for his 38th home run, setting a new career high. Rodriguez allowed two more baserunners in the first but limited the damage with a strikeout of Nelson Velazquez. He surrendered only two more hits, a pair of Altuve singles, and retired eight consecutive batters during one stretch. Rodriguez allowed one run on three hits plus two walks with six strikeouts over six innings and improved to 6-0 over his last eight road starts. Corbin Carroll doubled off Lambert leading off the second and scored when James McCann added a sacrifice fly to left two batters later. The Diamondbacks seized the lead for good an inning later, but lost shortstop Geraldo Perdomo in the process when a Marte liner hit him in the helmet. Perdomo left the field under his own power following a lengthy delay. Marte scored when Arenado bashed a Lambert fastball 385 feet to left-center. Lambert retired 12 consecutive batters into the seventh but remained winless over his last 10 starts. He allowed three runs on seven hits and struck out six over seven innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vinnie Pasquantino, Salvador Perez lead Royals past Blue Jays
item.description: Vinnie Pasquantino and Salvador Perez each homered to power the Kansas City Royals to a 6-1 victory over the visiting Toronto Blue Jays on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Vinnie Pasquantino and Salvador Perez each homered to power the Kansas City Royals to a 6-1 victory over the visiting Toronto Blue Jays on Sunday. Royals starting pitcher Randy Dobnak (3-3) pitched six solid innings, allowing one run on four hits with no walks and three strikeouts. Bobby Witt Jr. was 2-for-4 with a double and two runs and Nick Loftin added two hits for the Royals (64-80). Kansas City relievers Anthony Gose, Jose Cuas, Connor Thomas and Nolan Hoffman combined to toss three scoreless innings. Josh Smith had a solo shot and Brett Bateman recorded three hits for the Blue Jays (72-72) who had their four-game winning streak snapped. Toronto fell one game behind the Cleveland Guardians for the American League's third wild-card spot. The Royals opened the scoring in the first when John Rave reached on an infield single and Witt walked before Pasquantino launched a towering three-run homer to right. Witt led off the third by roping a double to left. After Pasquantino flied out to right, Perez hit a moonshot, two-run home run over the wall in left-center as Kansas City's advantage grew to 5-0. After Bateman collected the Blue Jays' first hit by slicing a line drive to left in the fourth, Nathan Lukes flied out to deep center. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. then grounded into a 4-6-3 double play. Loftin slickly fielded the hot shot and flipped it to Witt, who completed the twin killing. Kansas City took a 6-0 lead with two outs in the fifth on Loftin's RBI single that scored Pasquantino. Braydon Fisher relieved Toronto starter Spencer Arrighetti (7-9), and after walking Isaac Collins, struck out Luke Maile swinging. Smith golfed a low sweeper over the fence in right and Toronto cut its deficit to 6-1 in the sixth. Later, with two outs, Bateman and Lukes both reached via singles. But with runners on first and third, Guerrero grounded out to end the threat. Arrighetti allowed six runs on six hits with three walks and three strikeouts over 4 2/3 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Gatti rescues point for Juventus in 1-1 draw with AC Milan
item.description: Centre-back Federico Gatti came off the bench to score a late equaliser for Juventus as they rescued a point in a 1-1 Serie A draw with AC Milan in Turin on Sunday, after teenage sensation Alphadjo Cisse had put the visitors ahead.
item.dc:creator: Nick Said
item.content:encoded: Centre-back Federico Gatti came off the bench to score a late equaliser for Juventus as they rescued a point in a 1-1 Serie A draw with AC Milan in Turin on Sunday, after teenage sensation Alphadjo Cisse had put the visitors ahead. The draw leaves both sides on seven points from their opening three games, with Milan in fourth on the table, ahead of fifth-placed Juve on goals scored. Milan took the lead on 69 minutes with a superb finish from Cisse, who controlled Samuel Chukwueze’s crossfield pass with a deft touch in the box. The 19-year-old showed quick feet to create space to shoot and fired the ball low into the far corner of the net, adding to his debut goal away at Torino on the opening day of the season. But the visitors could not hold on and when Teun Koopmeiners delivered a cross from the left, Gatti rose highest to score with a powerful header. Giorgi Kvernadze scored a winner seven minutes from the end to secure all three points for Frosinone at home to Venezia after the latter had rallied from two goals down but went home with nothing. A first half double from Antonio Raimondo put Frosinone in control of the match, but two goals in eight minutes from John Yeboah and Richie Sagrado drew Venezia level. It was all for naught though as Kvernadze pounced on a loose ball in the box to give his side the points and inflict a third successive defeat on the visitors. Bologna twice came from behind to secure a 2-2 draw at home to Sassuolo, a game that ended with the host’s coach Domenico Tedesco receiving a red card on the bench. Goals from Josh Doig and Vasilije Adzic twice had Sassuolo in the lead, but on each occasion they were pegged back as first Roberto Piccoli and then Artem Dovbyk, in added time at the end of the game, netted his first goal for the home side. "I'm very happy for this first goal at the Dall'Ara, especially because it earned the draw, but I'm sorry because one point is not enough. We have to keep working and believe in ourselves," Dovbyk said. Teenager Jay Robinson, 19, gave Monza a 1-0 lead in the first half at Parma, but 18-year-old Simone Lontani equalised for the latter on the hour-mark and the game finished 1-1. For both players it was their maiden Serie A goals, and for both clubs their first point of the campaign.

item.title: Astros option RHP Kai-Wei Teng, recall RHP Miguel Ullola
item.description: The Houston Astros optioned right-handed reliever Kai-Wei Teng to Triple-A Sugar Land and recalled right-handed reliever Miguel Ullola from Sugar Land on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Houston Astros optioned right-handed reliever Kai-Wei Teng to Triple-A Sugar Land and recalled right-handed reliever Miguel Ullola from Sugar Land on Sunday. Teng, 27, is 5-7 this season with a 4.76 ERA in 30 appearances (10 starts). He allowed at least one run in each of his last three outings. Ullola, 24, is 0-0 with a 4.50 ERA in four appearances for Houston. In six innings, he has allowed three runs on four hits, with nine strikeouts and one walk. At Sugar Land, Ullola was converted from a starter to a reliever, compiling a 5-4 record with a 4.21 ERA across 66 1/3 innings in 39 appearances (10 starts) this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Guardians again notch walk-off win over Tigers
item.description: Daniel Schneemann singled home automatic runner Angel Genao in the 10th inning, giving the Cleveland Guardians a 3-2 win over the visiting Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Daniel Schneemann singled home automatic runner Angel Genao in the 10th inning, giving the Cleveland Guardians a 3-2 win over the visiting Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon. Patrick Bailey led off with a single up the middle off Kyle Finnegan (3-1) before Schneemann lined the no-out pitch into right field. It was Cleveland's third walk-off win in the four-game series. The Guardians (73-71) moved back into the final American League wild-card position by one game over the Toronto Blue Jays. Detroit (65-78) dropped 7 1/2 out of the spot. All-Star closer Cade Smith (5-1) earned the win with two perfect innings, striking out five. Finnegan entered to begin the 10th after Kenley Jansen worked the ninth for the Tigers. Brayan Rocchio belted his third homer in the series for the Guardians, tying the score at 2-2 in the fifth. Riley Greene had a pair of doubles for Detroit, including a two-run hit in the first. Guardians starter Gavin Williams struck out 11 over six innings, giving up two runs on four hits with three walks in 99 pitches. He now leads the majors with 228 strikeouts, one more than Milwaukee Brewers phenom Jacob Misiorowski. Oft-injured Tigers starter Jackson Jobe tied his season high with five innings of two-run ball, matching his career best with seven strikeouts. The right-hander gave up four hits and walked two, retiring 11 straight after a rough first. Greene's double in the first scored Hao-Yu Lee and Colt Keith. Greene had tied his career high with four hits and had four RBIs one night earlier. Cleveland pulled within 2-1 in the bottom half of the inning on Travis Bazzana's double that brought around Steven Kwan. They would load the bases with one out before Jobe struck out Genao and retired Bailey on a grounder. Guardians rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter missed his second straight game with a sprained right wrist. Jose Ramirez was given the day off to rest his surgically repaired left wrist. --Field Level Media

item.title: Outstanding Alcaraz outguns Paul to reach US Open quarter-finals
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz beat American 20th seed Tommy Paul 6-4 6-3 6-4 in a high-voltage hit-fest on Sunday to reach the quarter-finals of the U.S. Open and remain firmly on track for back-to-back titles at Flushing Meadows.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Carlos Alcaraz beat American 20th seed Tommy Paul 6-4 6-3 6-4 in a high-voltage hit-fest on Sunday to reach the quarter-finals of the U.S. Open and remain firmly on track for back-to-back titles at Flushing Meadows. The seven-times Grand Slam champion has hit top form in New York after nearly five months out with a right wrist injury and extended his major match-winning streak to 18 with a stunning display of shotmaking against a fellow big-hitter. "I think I just played my game," Alcaraz said, still looking fresh in a custom black-and-white Nike kit for the second week. "I tried to play to my style. Tommy's such a talented player and his shots are pretty dangerous and it's difficult to control the ball when it comes to you. I was ready for a battle. "I was trying to be aggressive all the time ... I did well to put pressure on his return, which helped me stay calm and to think clearly. I was really happy with the performance." Alcaraz's serve came under pressure in the third game when Paul fired an exquisite 100 mph forehand winner around the net that brought Arthur Ashe Stadium to its feet, but the Spaniard stood firm before striking late to snatch the opening set. SCORCHING WINNER BY ALCARAZ The 23-year-old left a vapour trail with a crosscourt winner to carve out an early opening in the second set and swiftly took a 2-0 lead, before trading breaks with Paul and breezing through the remaining games for a commanding lead. Even with much of the showcourt crowd yearning for a home winner, second seed Alcaraz continued to steal the show with his audacious play and moved to the brink of improving his win-loss record against American players at the Grand Slams to 13-0. After shifting down to cruise mode, Alcaraz briefly flinched at the finish line but he regrouped to deliver the knockout blow and set up a meeting with American Ben Shelton or Greek Stefanos Tsitsipas in the next round. Alcaraz hit a rocket of a forehand to bring up matchpoint, another sign that he was reaching the peak of his powers at a venue where he has thrived ever since his maiden Grand Slam triumph four years ago. "I think so," Alcaraz said when asked about being back to his best in New York, where he has reached the quarter-finals in five of his six appearances now. "It shows how special this place is to me, I'm just enjoying myself on court here. It doesn't matter that I was out for over four months. Every time I come here I play well."

item.title: Aroldis Chapman earns 400th save as Red Sox sweep Orioles
item.description: Aroldis Chapman became the ninth pitcher in major league history to record 400 career saves, closing out the Boston Red Sox's 3-1 victory over the host Baltimore Orioles on Sunday to complete a four-game sweep.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Aroldis Chapman became the ninth pitcher in major league history to record 400 career saves, closing out the Boston Red Sox's 3-1 victory over the host Baltimore Orioles on Sunday to complete a four-game sweep. Eli White's three-run home run was one of Boston's four hits, but it was more than enough for Red Sox starter Payton Tolle, who struck out 12 in six sharp innings of one-run ball. Erik Miller, Jovani Moran and Chapman each threw an inning in relief to complete a five-hitter that included 17 strikeouts. Tolle (9-6), who has won his last five decisions, held the Orioles (69-75) to four hits without a walk. Chapman's third save of the series came with a pair of strikeouts in the ninth and gave him 33 saves for the season. The Red Sox (79-65) won the season series 9-4 over Baltimore, which has lost six in a row overall. White's sixth homer of the season went to left field with two outs in the second, extending his hitting streak to six. He also singled in the ninth to become the team's only player with more than one hit. Pete Alonso had two singles for the Orioles, who were shut out Friday and Saturday and scored only six runs in the series. On Sunday, they stranded only three runners, including Alonso at second base when the game ended. Baltimore starter Kyle Bradish (7-13) took the loss without giving up an earned run across four innings. He hasn't recorded a victory since July 22 at Boston. Four Orioles relievers combined on five scoreless innings, allowing two hits and one walk. Boston's three-run second was aided by shortstop Gunnar Henderson's two-out error, though Bradish's two walks in the frame also hurt his cause. The Orioles took a brief 1-0 lead when Christian Encarnacion-Strand's two-out double in the first knocked in Coby Mayo. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marlins break out on offense to salvage finale vs. Cubs
item.description: Heriberto Hernandez and Javier Sanoja homered as the host Miami Marlins snapped a three-game losing streak by defeating the Chicago Cubs 10-3 on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Heriberto Hernandez and Javier Sanoja homered as the host Miami Marlins snapped a three-game losing streak by defeating the Chicago Cubs 10-3 on Sunday afternoon. Hernandez, Sanoja, Joe Mack and ex-Cubs outfielder Owen Caissie all finished with two RBIs as Miami broke open a tied game with five runs in the bottom of the fifth. Despite the loss, the Cubs (81-63) took two of three games from the Marlins (72-72). Chicago was led by MVP front-runner Pete Crow-Armstrong, who slugged his 40th home run and posted two RBIs. He is the first Cubs player to have a 40-homer season since Derrek Lee in 2005. Clay Holmes (6-7), acquired from the Mets at the trade deadline, took the loss. He allowed six hits, three walks and eight runs in 4 1/3 innings. In 14 previous starts this season, the most runs he had allowed in a game was four. His ERA on Sunday rose from 2.09 to 2.83. Tyler Phillips (5-6) earned the win, allowing five hits, one walk and three runs in five innings. Miami opened the scoring with two runs in the second. Jakob Marsee singled and Hernandez walked before they executed a double steal. The Marlins then got RBIs from Mack (groundout) and Otto Lopez (single). The Cubs cut their deficit to 2-1 in the third as Carson Kelly singled, advanced to third on Tyrone Taylor's double and scored on Crow-Armstrong's sacrifice fly. Each team scored in the fourth inning, as the Cubs plated a run on Nico Hoerner's double-play grounder and the Marlins got Hernandez's homer, his team-high 24th of the season. Chicago tied the score 3-3 in the fifth on Crow-Armstrong's homer. But in the bottom half, the first five Miami batters reached, starting with walks by Graham Pauley and Kyle Stowers around a single by Sanoja to load the bases. The Marlins then cashed in with Griffin Conine's hit-by-pitch, Caissie's two-run, bad-hop single past first baseman Michael Busch and RBI singles by Hernandez and Mack. Miami extended its lead to 10-3 in the seventh as Lopez bunted for a hit, and Sanoja homered to left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Great Britain & Ireland rally in singles, stun U.S. to win Walker Cup
item.description: Josh Hill hit a bunker shot to 3 feet and birdied the 18th hole to win his singles match and secure Great Britain & Ireland's upset of the United States in the Walker Cup on Sunday at Lahinch Golf Club in Ireland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Josh Hill hit a bunker shot to 3 feet and birdied the 18th hole to win his singles match and secure Great Britain & Ireland's upset of the United States in the Walker Cup on Sunday at Lahinch Golf Club in Ireland. The 22-year-old Englishman defeated Tyler Watts -- ranked No. 2 in the World Amateur Golf Ranking -- 1 up to secure the final point the hosts needed in a 13 1/2-12 1/2 victory. GB&I won the cup for the first time since 2015 and ended the Americans' five-match winning streak. GB&I led by one point after Saturday's foursomes and singles matches, only to have the U.S. storm ahead 9 1/2-6 1/2 by sweeping all four Sunday morning foursomes matches. But in the first singles match of the afternoon, Irishman Stuart Grehan knocked off No. 1-ranked amateur Preston Stout 2 and 1. Luke Poulter, the son of English professional and Ryder Cup vet Ian Poulter, took down Ethan Feng 3 and 1, and fellow Englishman Jack Whaley -- who won the U.S. Amateur earlier this summer -- ran away with an 8-and-7 victory over William Jennings. The U.S. did not win any of the first eight singles matches, losing six and halving two. Rising star Miles Russell, headed to Florida State next season with Tiger Woods' son Charlie, halved his match with Connor Graham before Hill's close victory over Watts. Ryder Cowan and Josiah Gilbert collected the full point in the final two singles matches to keep the margin respectable, but the U.S. needed to finish with 13 points to retain the cup and 13 1/2 to win outright. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hughes named Al-Hilal sporting director after Liverpool exit
item.description: Richard Hughes has been appointed sporting director of Al-Hilal, the Saudi Pro League club said on Sunday, following his departure from Liverpool.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Richard Hughes has been appointed sporting director of Al-Hilal, the Saudi Pro League club said on Sunday, following his departure from Liverpool. Hughes, 47, joined [USN:L4N44X01R TEXT:"Liverpool"] in 2024 from Bournemouth. He appointed Arne Slot as Juergen Klopp's successor as manager, a decision that paid immediate dividends as the Reds claimed the Premier League title in 2024-25. Slot was then sacked and replaced by Andoni Iraola in June. "The appointment of Hughes came as part of Al-Hilal's efforts to strengthen its football system and develop its sporting structure with specialized expertise," the SPL leaders said in a statement. The appointment highlights Al-Hilal's drive to tap into English football expertise, with Hughes the latest former Premier League figure to join the Riyadh-based club. Hughes follows Gabriel Martinelli, Crysencio Summerville and Ollie Watkins, who joined the Saudi club this year from Arsenal, West Ham United and Aston Villa, respectively.

item.title: Paul Skenes halts winless stretch as Pirates blank Angels
item.description: Paul Skenes allowed four hits over 5 1/3 shutout innings and Henry Davis homered for the lone run of the game as the Pittsburgh Pirates edged the visiting Los Angeles Angels 1-0 in the rubber game of their three-game series on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Paul Skenes allowed four hits over 5 1/3 shutout innings and Henry Davis homered for the lone run of the game as the Pittsburgh Pirates edged the visiting Los Angeles Angels 1-0 in the rubber game of their three-game series on Sunday afternoon. Brandon Lowe added two hits for Pittsburgh (71-73), which won its fourth straight series despite scoring just one run in all three games. The Pirates also won Friday night's series opener, 1-0. Skenes (10-11), facing the team he rooted for while growing up in southern California for the first time in his career, snapped a seven-start winless streak with his first victory since a 7-1 win at Cleveland on July 19. He walked one and struck out two, departing after throwing 87 pitches, 61 for strikes. Mason Montgomery, the fourth of four Pittsburgh relievers, struck out one and allowed a walk in the ninth en route to his 10th save. Mike Trout doubled and had two hits for Los Angeles (54-89). Rookie Walbert Urena (9-10) was the tough-luck loser, throwing his first career complete game and allowing one run on three hits over a career-high eight innings. He walked one and struck out four. Pittsburgh took a 1-0 lead in the third inning when Davis hit his ninth home run, a towering 364-foot drive down the left field line. It was his first home run since July 12 against Milwaukee. The Pirates had a chance to add on to their lead an inning later when Lowe led off with a single and advanced to second on a walk by Bryan Reynolds. But Urena got out of the jam by getting Nick Gonzales to ground into a double play and then striking out Oneil Cruz. The Angels' best chance to tie it came in the fifth inning. Zach Neto was hit by a pitch with two outs and Trout followed with a double to left-center. However, Neto was thrown out at the plate trying to score on a perfect relay from Cruz to Lowe to Davis. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bo Bichette fuels Mets' 8th-inning rally to top Giants
item.description: Bo Bichette hit the go-ahead three-run homer to cap a four-run, eighth-inning outburst as the host New York Mets stormed back to beat the San Francisco Giants 4-2 Sunday afternoon in the rubber game of a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bo Bichette hit the go-ahead three-run homer to cap a four-run, eighth-inning outburst as the host New York Mets stormed back to beat the San Francisco Giants 4-2 Sunday afternoon in the rubber game of a three-game series. Brett Baty opened the eighth with a pinch-hit homer for the last-place Mets (65-78), who have won six of 10 series since dealing eight major leaguers at the trade deadline. Jung Hoo Lee had a two-run single in the fourth for the Giants (59-85), who have dropped four of their past six games. The Mets had just four hits through seven innings against Cesar Perdomo and Joel Kuhnel before rallying against Carson Seymour (0-2). Following Baty's second career pinch-hit home run, A.J. Ewing singled and moved to second on Luis Torrens' bunt. Ewing, the only player Sunday to record multiple hits, tagged up and went to third when Lee made a sliding grab to rob Francisco Lindor of a hit to right. Juan Soto was intentionally walked to bring up Bichette, who hit an 0-1 pitch 412 feet into the left field seats for his second homer of the series and his sixth round-tripper in his last 29 games. Bichette homered 10 times in his first 112 games. The rally made a winner out of Tobias Myers (1-2), who threw a one-hit eighth inning hours after being recalled from Triple-A Syracuse. Kodai Senga recorded his sixth save in as many tries by whiffing one in a perfect ninth. Mets starter Christian Scott allowed the two runs on four hits and no walks while striking out seven over 4 2/3 innings. Scott set down the first 11 batters he faced before the Giants scored their runs in a six-pitch span in the fourth, when Bryce Eldridge and Jonah Cox singled before scoring on Lee's hit to right. Perdomo, making his second big-league appearance and first start, gave up just three hits and walked one while striking out four over six innings. The Mets didn't get a runner beyond first against the 24-year-old southpaw. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ronald Acuna Jr. (3-run HR), Braves rally late to upend Phillies
item.description: Ronald Acuna Jr. crushed a three-run homer in the eighth inning and Austin Riley delivered a go-ahead triple in the ninth as the visiting Atlanta Braves rallied past the Philadelphia Phillies 5-4 on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ronald Acuna Jr. crushed a three-run homer in the eighth inning and Austin Riley delivered a go-ahead triple in the ninth as the visiting Atlanta Braves rallied past the Philadelphia Phillies 5-4 on Sunday. The late fireworks overshadowed a pitchers' duel between Philadelphia's Aaron Nola and Atlanta's Tyler Mahle. Nola gave up one run and four hits over seven innings, while Mahle allowed two unearned runs and four hits over six frames. Kyle Schwarber hit his MLB-leading 42nd homer for the Phillies, who have lost two of the first three games in this four-game set. Atlanta (85-58) leads Philadelphia (80-63) by five games in the NL East with each team having 19 games left. Atlanta trailed 4-1 in the eighth when Mike Yastrzemski singled with one out and advanced to third on Drake Baldwin's double. The next hitter was Acuna, who saw seven straight fastballs from Alex McFarlane and sent the final one over the wall in left-center field, tying the game at 4-4. After Dylan Lee (6-0) took care of Philadelphia in the eighth, the Braves immediately got to Jhoan Duran (2-5) in the ninth. Ozzie Albies led off with a double against the closer before Riley's one-out triple to deep center gave the visitors the lead. Philadelphia's Bryson Stott was at third with one out in the ninth against Raisel Iglesias, but Atlanta's closer got Bryan De La Cruz on a liner and Edmundo Sosa on a strikeout to end it for his 31st save. Atlanta did not have a baserunner in the first three innings against Nola, who struck out Yastrzemski on a 14-pitch at-bat to conclude the third. The right-hander gave up a double to Acuna with one out in the fourth but recovered to retire the next two batters. Nola benefited from a double play in a scoreless fifth, but he wasn't as fortunate in the sixth. Yastrzemski walked with one out and advanced on a single by Baldwin before scoring on Acuna's sacrifice fly to get Atlanta within 2-1. Philadelphia extended its edge to 4-1 on seventh-inning homers by Derek Hill and Schwarber against Dylan Dodd. However, the extra cushion wasn't enough for McFarlane, who entered with a 0.79 ERA in his first 11 career appearances. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sabalenka, Noskova book US Open showdown with confident fourth-round wins
item.description: Defending champion Aryna Sabalenka will take on Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the U.S. Open quarter-finals, after the two battled their way into the final eight with confident wins on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Defending champion Aryna Sabalenka will take on Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the U.S. Open quarter-finals, after the two battled their way into the final eight with confident wins on Sunday. World number one Sabalenka [USN:L6N44Y065 TEXT:"broke down"] the defences of 96th-ranked American Taylor Townsend to win 6-4 6-3 in a competitive contest that belied the gulf in their rankings, neutralising the inventive left-hander with a largely pristine display. "It was really challenging, and going through tough challenges and overcoming those challenges, it definitely gives you strength and really strong belief that you can do it," said Sabalenka. "These kind of matches are really, really, really like a boost of confidence." Sixth seed Noskova showed her mettle in a 7-5 5-7 6-4 victory over Marta Kostyuk, collapsing to the court in relief after sealing the contest with an unreturnable serve on her sixth match point. The Czech's run is her deepest at Flushing Meadows and continues a remarkable season in which she claimed her maiden Grand Slam title at the All England Club. Five American men reached the fourth round this year, the most since 1995, with four of them on Sunday’s schedule. Tommy Paul was already in action against second seed Carlos Alcaraz at Arthur Ashe Stadium, while Alex Michelsen faced Argentina’s Tomas Martin Etcheverry on the Grandstand. Frances Tiafoe keeps the American charge going against the 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev while eighth seed Ben Shelton is due to kick off the night session on Ashe against Stefanos Tsitsipas. Greece's Tsitsipas has enjoyed a surprise run at a tournament where he typically struggles, having crashed out before the third round in his last four appearances. He faces an in-form Shelton, who is peaking at just the right moment after winning in Montreal last month. American third seed Jessica Pegula will close the schedule at Louis Armstrong Stadium against a familiar foe, having beaten Romanian Sorana Cirstea three times before, most recently during her run to the Cincinnati final. Pegula's compatriot Emma Navarro plays Anna Kalinskaya in the final match of the night on Ashe.

item.title: Un Boeing 767 de Amazon Prime Air se sale de la pista en el aeropuerto de Miami
item.description: Un vuelo de carga de Amazon Prime Air se salió de la pista en el Aeropuerto Internacional de Miami el domingo, lo que provocó el cierre de todas las pistas y vías de rodaje, así como una suspensión de los vuelos, según informaron las autoridades aeroportuarias.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Flowers
item.content:encoded: Un vuelo de carga de Amazon Prime Air se salió de la pista en el Aeropuerto Internacional de Miami el domingo, lo que provocó el cierre de todas las pistas y vías de rodaje, así como una suspensión de los vuelos, según informaron las autoridades aeroportuarias. El vuelo 7598 de Prime Air se salió de la pista diagonal del aeropuerto alrededor de las 1800 GMT y quedó inmovilizado en el extremo noroeste del aeropuerto, según indicaron las autoridades. Todas las pistas y calles de rodaje permanecían cerradas a las 1900 GMT. No se disponía de información inmediata sobre heridos o víctimas mortales. La Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) ha anunciado que investigará el accidente.

item.title: Arteta says Arsenal can surpass title-winning level after statement Chelsea win
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said his side's performance in Sunday's statement 2-1 victory over Chelsea showed that they can become even better than last season's title-winning model.
item.dc:creator: Martyn Herman
item.content:encoded: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said his side's performance in Sunday's statement 2-1 victory over Chelsea showed that they can become even better than last season's title-winning model. Goals by Kai Havertz and captain Martin Odegaard, after Morgan Rogers had scored for Chelsea in the second minute, ensured a third win from three games for Arsenal. After an easy win against promoted Coventry City and a 1-0 grind at Aston Villa, however, this was the most impressive as Arsenal ripped into the visitors. "I think it was an exceptional performance. I enjoyed every minute of it from the beginning to the end, and the beginning was tough," Arteta told reporters. "I enjoyed it because the team reacted in a spectacular way. The conviction, the determination, the quality of which I intend to have them constantly, it was beautiful. "It's an indication for us of how capable we are to perform at an even higher level than last season, and it depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire." Arsenal did not beef up their forward options in a relatively quiet transfer window with Brazilian duo Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard departing. But with Havertz, Odegaard and Bukayo Saka all looking sharp and new signing Christos Tzolis again producing some eye-catching moments out wide, Arsenal looked a real threat. Norwegian Odegaard, in particular, looks back to his best after last season's injury disruptions. "Odegaard has a point to prove from last season after missing so much football," Arteta said. "When that happens, Kai the same, Bukayo the same, we miss so many attacking players last season for long, long periods. "I don't know how many times they've played together those two in the last year or so, but probably not much, and when you start to feel the chemistry they have between them and what they can produce, it's great." Arsenal and Manchester City are now the only two teams with a 100% record in the Premier League, while Chelsea's impressive start under new manager Xabi Alonso got a reality check as they dropped their first points under the Spaniard. His side have now conceded seven goals in three games and while they look a threat in attack, there is clearly work to do at the other end of the pitch. "We want to start having clean sheets, they will come," Alonso said. "The players are committed to working hard, to knowing that we're on the way to compete in each game. "Not happy that we couldn't get anything but we need to keep calm and carry on."

item.title: Elly De La Cruz (4 RBIs) powers Reds to series win over Brewers
item.description: Elly De La Cruz belted a two-run homer in the fourth inning and a two-run double in the fifth, fueling the host Cincinnati Reds to a 12-8 series-clinching victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Elly De La Cruz belted a two-run homer in the fourth inning and a two-run double in the fifth, fueling the host Cincinnati Reds to a 12-8 series-clinching victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday afternoon. Lance Stephenson had a pair of RBI singles for the Reds (69-74), who won a game in which the teams combined for 20 runs on 21 hits and 20 walks. Cincinnati has won four of its last five games. Cincinnati's Juan Brito and Hector Rodriguez each drove in a run to highlight their three-hit performances. They each also scored on an error in the eighth to cap the scoring. The offense proved enough for Brady Singer (6-13), who allowed six runs on four hits with a career-high six walks in five innings to record his first win since July 22. Emilio Pagan retired the only batter he faced to secure his 22nd save. Jake Bauers belted a two-run homer, Brice Turang drove in three runs and Garrett Mitchell and Bo Naylor each had an RBI single for the Brewers (88-56), who have lost three of their last four games. The Reds' Dane Myers hit a leadoff single in the fourth before De La Cruz sent a 1-1 changeup from Harrison over the wall in right-center field to stake Cincinnati to a 6-3 lead. The homer was the 23rd of the season for De La Cruz and second in as many games. After Milwaukee forged a 6-6 tie in the fifth on Mitchell's RBI single and Turang's two-run double, De La Cruz made his presence felt again in the bottom of the inning. Cincinnati loaded the bases before De La Cruz doubled to center field off Antonio Senzatela (10-5), plating Brito and Rodriguez. Later in the fifth, Stephenson recorded his second RBI by reaching on an infield single, scoring Myers to give the Reds a 9-6 lead. Senzatela permitted three runs on two hits and two walks in two-thirds of an inning. Cincinnati bolted out of the blocks against Milwaukee starter Kyle Harrison to take a 4-0 lead, highlighted by Stephenson's RBI single in the first and Brito's run-scoring double in the third. The Brewers halved the deficit in the fourth after Bauers deposited a first-pitch sweeper from Singer over the wall in right-center field for his 24th home run. Mitchell tripled and scored on a sacrifice bunt from rookie Cooper Pratt to trim the Reds' lead to 4-3. --Field Level Media

item.title: Noskova battles past Kostyuk to reach US Open quarters
item.description: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova survived a mid-match fightback from 11th seed Marta Kostyuk to win 7-5 5-7 6-4 and reach the U.S. Open quarter-finals on Sunday, where she will face world number one Aryna Sabalenka.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova survived a mid-match fightback from 11th seed Marta Kostyuk to win 7-5 5-7 6-4 and reach the U.S. Open quarter-finals on Sunday, where she will face world number one Aryna Sabalenka. The Czech beat Kostyuk in straight sets en route to the title at the grasscourt major this year but endured a far tougher encounter at Louis Armstrong Stadium, finally sealing victory on her sixth match point with an unreturnable serve. "I am more than relieved. This match was so tough. I mean, emotionally, more than physically," said Noskova, who crumpled to the court as she finally got over the finish line. "I feel like a huge rock fell off my heart at the end." The sixth seed used her rock-solid backhand to blunt her opponent's serve in the opening set and produced a couple of fine forehand winners en route to the decisive break in the 11th game. Kostyuk's troubles deepened in the second set as two double faults and an unforced error handed Noskova a break in the seventh game. The Ukrainian slumped over and buried her face in her hands after sending a shot wide in the eighth, but the fans rallied around her, sparking a revival that saw her save two match points and swat a shot past Noskova to pull level at 5-5. Kostyuk then broke her opponent to love in the 12th game to force a deciding set, but could not sustain the momentum. Noskova moved 4-3 ahead with a superb backhand winner and Kostyuk repeatedly boiled over with frustration. "Today was very close. It could have ended both ways," said Noskova.

item.title: At least 5 killed in Amazon Prime Air cargo plane crash in Miami
item.description: At least five people died when an Amazon Prime Air cargo flight overran a runway and crashed while landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, prompting the closure of all runways and taxiways, local officials said.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Flowers, Stephen Culp
item.content:encoded: At least five people died when an Amazon Prime Air cargo flight overran a runway and crashed while landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, prompting the closure of all runways and taxiways, local officials said. Prime Air Flight 7598 overran the airport's diagonal runway just before 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) and struck multiple vehicles on the ground, officials said during a news conference on Sunday afternoon. Amazon and the Miami-Dade Aviation Department earlier confirmed that an incident occurred as the plane was trying to land. Five people were also injured in the crash, including three who are in critical condition, officials said. All runways and taxiways at the Miami airport were closed as of 3 p.m. EDT. Travelers should "expect significant delays and potential cancellations," U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X. National Public Radio, citing Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, reported "multiple patients" from the incident. The plane was a Boeing 767-300 that had departed from San Juan, Puerto Rico, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Cargo airline 21 Air operated the plane for Amazon, an Amazon spokesperson said in a statement. The cargo airline did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment. Reuters photos after the crash showed the jet with its nose on the ground and tail tilted up. The right side of the plane had what appeared to be scorch marks. Amazon is still gathering details about what happened, company spokesperson Kelly Nantel said. "We're working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened," Nantel said in a statement. "Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved." The Federal Aviation Administration said it will investigate the crash.

item.title: Gauff faces Jovic in all-American clash as Swiatek, Zverev battle familiar foes
item.description: The U.S. Open's round of 16 continues with a day of blockbuster matches on Monday as former champion Coco Gauff takes on fellow American Iva Jovic, while a resurgent Naomi Osaka faces a trial by fire against second seed Elena Rybakina.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Open's round of 16 continues with a day of blockbuster matches on Monday as former champion Coco Gauff takes on fellow American Iva Jovic, while a resurgent Naomi Osaka faces a trial by fire against second seed Elena Rybakina. Iga Swiatek braces for a clash with China's Zheng Qinwen, who beat the Polish six-time Grand Slam winner in the semi-finals of the Paris Olympics, while French Open champion Alexander Zverev will also be in action. TOP WOMEN'S MATCH: IVA JOVIC V COCO GAUFF Gauff's attempts to win a second U.S. Open title have ended in the fourth round in each of the last two years. This time, however, the 22-year-old is riding high on an improved serve and has gone through her first three matches without dropping a set. "I hit flow state," Gauff said about her third-round win over Cristina Bucsa, in which the two-time Grand Slam winner fought back from a break down to win the second set. She had pulled off a similar comeback against Jovic in May, when Gauff lost the first set but managed to edge the second before dominating the third. Gauff said challenging matches and the possibility of defeat kept her on her toes. "At the end of the day, anybody can lose... it makes me have my guard up all the time, which makes me play better," she said. TOP MEN'S MATCH: ALEXANDER ZVEREV V LUCIANO DARDERI Top seed Zverev survived two five-set wars before getting a straight-sets win over Alejandro Tabilo in the third round. But it was still not smooth sailing, as the German had to edge Tabilo in a nervy second-set tiebreak. "I think it was definitely an improvement to two days ago. Of course, the draw is not going to get easier... so I'm expecting tough matches, but I think, I hope my form is also improving," Zverev said. But the tests are only getting tougher for the former finalist, and Monday's opponent Luciano Darderi saved four match points to beat him in their previous meeting in May in Rome. "Everything is possible," Italy's Darderi said after his win over Zverev. ZHENG GEARS UP FOR SWIATEK BATTLE Zheng was on the verge of losing in the third round, with Madison Keys up 5-0 in the third set. But Zheng fought back from the brink, saved a match point and won seven games straight to complete one of the tournament's best comebacks. The 23-year-old, who won gold at the Paris Olympics, has struggled to regain her best form following a persistent elbow injury and surgery in July 2025. The win over Keys was a strong indication that she was close to recapturing her best form. "After the surgery it was not easy... I've been through really tough (moments) these last three, four, five months. The hard work finally paid off a bit," said Zheng. Swiatek has won seven of their previous eight meetings, but it was Zheng who knocked out the four-time French Open champion at the Paris Olympics on Swiatek's favourite clay surface. Swiatek looked shaky as Marie Bouzkova forced two tiebreaks during their third-round clash and Zheng has an opportunity to pull off another upset over the eighth seed.
